Evaluate replayable mismatched-template draws

Source: R/reference_scoring.R
mismatch_draws.Rd

Evaluate replayable mismatched-template draws

Usage

mismatch_draws(
  strata,
  refs,
  n = 100,
  trial = "trial",
  seed = 1,
  assignments = NULL,
  replace_ref = c("self_item", "all"),
  restandardize = TRUE,
  standardize = c("within_subject", "none"),
  by = c("fixation", "trial"),
  control_policy = c("exclude_replacement", "fixed")
)

Arguments

strata

A case-control table from sample_controls().

refs

A reference set.

n

Number of null draws.

trial

Trial column, nested within the reference subject column.

seed

Seed, or NULL to use the session RNG.

assignments

Saved output of mismatch_assignments(). If NULL, create n draws using seed; supplied assignments are evaluated without RNG use.

replace_ref

Replace only self_item or the entire reference tuple.

restandardize

Refit scaling in every null draw. FALSE applies the original observed fit. Each paired matched/mismatched comparison uses the same fit (estimated on retained mismatched scores when TRUE). This choice alone does not establish an exact randomization test: calibration also requires an appropriate exchangeability assumption.

standardize

Score standardization, as in score_strata().

by

Contrast resolution, as in case_control_contrast().

control_policy

By default, "exclude_replacement" removes observed controls donated by any trial of either the case's item or the replacement item, using the saved donor metadata. Cases are always retained. "fixed" retains all controls: this item-discrimination baseline can be negative under a genuine matched effect because it includes the replacement item's own test fixations.

Value

A list with observed contrasts on the original controls, paired_observed matched contrasts on each draw's retained controls and scaling, contrasts for mismatched templates, assignments, original observed scaling, and settings. Both paired tables carry null_draw and identical row keys. Compare paired_observed with contrasts to use the same controls and units. Evaluation proceeds one draw at a time.

Details

Exclusion uses donor items, including repeated trials of either item, rather than assuming trial labels equal item labels. It does not redraw controls. A stratum with no remaining controls is an error: a donor pool containing only the case and replacement items cannot support the paired comparison, regardless of the number of controls drawn. In particular, two test trials fail when they contain those two items. Generated uniform/map controls have no donor item and are retained. For older saved strata without donor metadata, complete case rows can supply the donor keys; otherwise resample and save the strata or choose the fixed policy. No automatic p-values or calibrated effect decomposition are computed.
